propositions: The enrich drain advisory lock is held across multi-minute LLM calls (437s, 131s observed), making the drain single-flight and causing child drains to skip with lock-held status, limiting throughput to ~5 items per multi-minute hold against an enqueue rate that produces a 1,046-entry backlog.

The restructured drain must split into three phases (collect under lock, enrich without lock, finalize without lock) with a concurrency guard capping live drainers at 3 distinct lease-holding IDs, releasing the lock before LLM calls to enable parallel batch processing.
The batch cap must be raised from 5 to 20 items and dynamically clamped to lease_ttl_s // 40 to prevent a single drain from outrunning its lease mid-run and exposing stale claims to expiry.

Stale-at-writeback revalidation must compare the ticket's content_hash at finalize against the snapshot taken at collect, skipping the digest emit and re-enqueueing with soak 0 if the ticket changed between phases.
Concurrent drains on the same ticket set must arbitrate claims to produce exactly one LLM call per ticket with no duplicates, validated by an instrumented re-entrant runner test.

The drain lock must never be held during any LLM call, validated by an instrumented runner that attempts to acquire the drain lock from inside every run() call and asserts success for all items in a batch.
